tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description begins with an imperative framing ('Diagnose...', and 'Use this skill when...') and enumerates a large number of explicit trigger symptoms and contexts (access denied, capacity errors, OOM, spot interruptions, lineage missing, MLflow failures, etc.), covering both training and registry domains. It also explicitly excludes an adjacent scope (evaluation jobs) to sharpen boundaries. It is dense but stays within a reasonable paragraph length and is focused on user-facing symptoms rather than internal implementation.
tests.evidence: "Diagnose an Amazon SageMaker training or customization job... Use this skill when a training job is denied access to S3, a KMS key or iam:PassRole, fails with InsufficientInstanceCapacity... Not for evaluation jobs of a fine-tuned model..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into domain-specific check IDs, APIs, and procedures (e.g., LLM-SM-TRAIN-001..008, REG-001..004) without explaining general concepts like what SageMaker or Model Registry are. It assumes agent familiarity and focuses on project-specific conventions.
tests.evidence: Every finding is grounded in the **LLM-SM** check family... load it before assigning any check-id or severity.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body contains only an index table of check-ids with one-line descriptions and a router table pointing to references; the detailed detection rules, remediations, and citations are explicitly deferred to references/checks-sagemaker-training.md.
tests.evidence: The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference; the table below is a what-it-catches index.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five reference files are linked with markdown links in the body (checks-sagemaker-training.md, collection-reference.md, api-quirks.md, known-causes.md, metrics-and-logs.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by clear conditions for when to load it, e.g. tied to specific symptoms or steps.
tests.evidence: Load [known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md) whenever the user names an error or symptom (training §1–§7, Model Registry §8–§14)

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (classification steps, severity assignment, read-only guardrails) are given exact prescriptive rules, while flexible parts (how to phrase remediation, how to assemble report) leave room for judgment with explained rationale.
tests.evidence: Classify **before** prescribing anything. Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill does not present competing tools as equal menus; it designates specific APIs per symptom as the clear path to follow (Router table), not a list of alternatives.
tests.evidence: | My training job failed, the data looks corrupt or won't parse | Training | `DescribeTrainingJob` `FailureReason`, then the JSONL sample | ...

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (classify area, describe job, bucket failure reason, confirm artifact, review registry, assemble report) applicable to any training job or package, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Classify **before** prescribing anything. Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist.
